title: Zwei Kisten
desc: A flat in a morning, and what goes in the boxes
setting: Three rooms, six people, and a van outside with the back doors open.

steps.speaker: Vreni
steps.es: Das kommt alles ins Brockenhaus. Ausser was in die Kisten geht.
steps.en: That is all going to the second-hand shop. Except what goes in the boxes.

options.en: What should go in the boxes?
options.feedback: Ask before you decide. It is her sister and they are her two boxes.
Nobody has offered you anything yet. Two hours later she does.
It is, and the rent runs on either way. She will tell you the arithmetic if you let her.

steps.speaker: Vreni
steps.es: Die Fotos vom Kasten. Legst du sie hinein?
steps.en: The photos from the sideboard. Will you put them in?

options.feedback: Say yes and put them in one at a time. She is watching, and that is the job.

options.en: Do you not want to do it yourself?
options.feedback: She asked you on purpose. She has been doing this since seven in the morning.

options.es: Der da ist ihr Mann, oder?
options.en: That one is her husband, isn't it?
options.feedback: It is, and now is not the hour for it. Ask her in a café in three weeks.

steps.speaker: Ruedi Zemp
steps.es: Nehmen Sie vorne, ich nehme hinten.
steps.en: You take the front, I will take the back.

options.feedback: He has carried furniture down this staircase for twenty years. Take the end you are given.

options.en: I can take the back as well.
options.feedback: You cannot, and he knows the second turn better than you do.

options.en: Should we do it with three?
options.feedback: Sensible for the cupboard. For a table it makes the stairs worse.
Stay for it. Standing in an empty kitchen with a paper cup is most of what today was for.
You took the day off. She knows, because you told her at eight.
Sie, still, after a morning of this. And it is a very large question for a paper cup.
